grammar.title: Reflexive Pronouns (myself) and Each Other
grammar.explanation:
We use **reflexive pronouns** like **myself**, **yourself**, **himself**, and **themselves** when the subject and the object are the same person. For example, I cut **myself**, and she taught **herself** to do a course online.

We use **each other** when two or more people do something to the other person. Tom and Anna love **each other**, and my sister and I phone **each other** every day.

Reflexive pronouns also add emphasis, meaning that person and nobody else. I fixed my bike **myself**, and the kids made breakfast **themselves**.

**By + reflexive** means alone, without help. She lives **by herself**, and the door closed **by itself**.

Some verbs do not need a reflexive pronoun. Say I **relaxed**, I **feel** tired, and I can't **concentrate**, not relaxed myself or feel myself.

Do not mix up **themselves** and **each other**. They looked at **themselves** means each person looked in a mirror, but they looked at **each other** means A looked at B and B looked at A.
examples: *We really enjoyed **ourselves** at the wedding.* (enjoy yourself)
*She lives **by herself** in a small flat.* (by herself = alone)
*My sister and I phone **each other** every day.* (each other)

practice.q: Rewrite with a reflexive pronoun: Sara did her homework alone, with no help.
practice.a: Sara did her homework by herself.

practice.q: Fix the mistake: He hurt him when he fell off his bike.
practice.a: He hurt himself when he fell off his bike.

practice.q: Fix the mistake: Tom and Anna love themselves. (Tom loves Anna and Anna loves Tom.)
practice.a: Tom and Anna love each other.

practice.q: Fix the mistake: I relaxed myself after work.
